Pero el viudo JUAN ANDRÉS y su hija LAURITA han tenido la misma idea. Por un error les alquilan la misma casa. La zona está llena por la temporada y se ven obligados a compartir el lugar, en principio por una noche. Pero una serie de circunstancias hacen que la situación se alargue. La magia navideña hace de las suyas y, poco a poco, entre ISABEL y JUAN ANDRÉS surge una atracción muy especial.

programme.title: Una Navidad Para Recordar
programme.desc: Sebastián detesta la navidad. Y esta le será particularmente difícil, puesto que es la primera que pasa sin sus hijos, después de un duro divorcio. Decide alejarse de la ciudad y pasar la temporada en la casa en que nació, visitando a su madre Ángela, que padece alzheimer. En esa breve y nostálgica temporada, SEBASTIÁN reencuentra la fe en la vida, se reconcilia con la familia, consigue un nuevo camino para el amor y recupera la emoción de la Navidad.

programme.title: Novios Por Navidad
programme.desc: VALERIA siempre soñó con una boda navideña. Y cuando se hizo planificadora de eventos, eso se convirtió en su sello. Cuando decidió casarse con BERNARDO planificó su boda para Diciembre. Pero no contaba con que TERE, su mejor amiga, terminaría robándole el novio y la idea. Tere le pide a Valeria que organicé su boda para navidad. Valeria acepta y decide presentarse a la boda del brazo del novio perfecto. Pero para ello necesita conseguir un novio con urgencia. Y no se le ocurre mejor idea que pedirle a CAMILO, el dueño de la finca colonial que han alquilado para la boda, que se haga pasar por su novio. Valeria y Camilo son polos opuestos, pero la magia de la navidad hace lo suyo y la mentira termina convirtiéndose en un inesperado romance.

programme.title: Intercambio Navideno
programme.desc: MAYA y ANA MARÍA son gemelas. Pero fueron separadas al nacer y entregadas a diferentes familias. Fueron criadas de maneras opuestas. ANA MARÍA es ahora una exitosa empresaria divorciada, que solo piensa en su éxito y en el trabajo. MAYA una incansable filántropa, criada por una familia que se dedica a trabajar en pro de los más necesitados. Ya adultas se descubren una a la otra y deciden guardar el secreto, para no hacer daño a sus familias. Pero una navidad deciden hacer la travesura de intercambiar sus vidas por una noche. Sin sospechar que aquella decisión las cambiará para siempre.

programme.title: Una Navidad Complicada
programme.desc: En medio de la temporada navideña, Leticia y Guillermo, divorciados desde hace años, enfrentan una situación inesperada cuando su hijo adolescente recurre a una trampa para reunirlos, falsificando un correo electrónico conde invita a Guillermo y su nueva novia a la casa familiar para Navidad. A medida que la forzada convivencia avanza, la relación entre Guillermo y su exesposa va cambiando. Guillermo descubre cuanto extraña su antigua vida, su vida familiar estable y hermosa. Y descubre que sigue amando a Leticia. Pero, para regresar definitivamente, necesita ganarse el perdón de Leticia y demostrarle que está dispuesto a cambiar. No es tan fácil, pero tal vez el espíritu navideño ayude a que suceda el milagro.

programme.title: El Sabor de la Navidad
programme.desc: Una pequeña empresa familiar de Rompope enfrenta una encrucijada cuando una transnacional decide cerrar sus puertas en plena temporada navideña. Gregorio, un ambicioso ejecutivo, es el encargado de supervisar el cierre de la empresa local. Pero, al llegar, es recibido con calidez y hospitalidad por los trabajadores de la empresa, especialmente por Erica, la directora de la planta, que cree que su intención es aumentar la producción. Poco a poco Gregorio se sumerge en la magia de la comunidad, comenzando a cuestionar sus propias lealtades y enamorándose del lugar y de Erica. programme.title: Una Navidad Para Recordar
programme.desc: Sebastián detesta la navidad. Y esta le será particularmente difícil, puesto que es la primera que pasa sin sus hijos, después de un duro divorcio. programme.title: Mi Amor en Navidad
programme.desc: LUCAS es un famoso cantante. Su tema navideño “Mi Amor en Navidad” ha sido un hit desde hace casi dos décadas. Pero ya no siente deseos de seguir interpretando esta canción. Un diciembre decide tomarse unas vacaciones para reflexionar sobre su carrera y sobre su futuro y regresa al pueblo donde creció. Allí se rencuentra con ELISA, su amor de juventud y conoce a JORGE, el hijo adolescente de ELISA, que sueña con llegar a ser músico. A través de ellos se conecta con sus raíces y sus recuerdos y consigue de nuevo esos motivos que una vez lo enamoraron de la música, de la navidad… ¡y de Elisa!

programme.title: El Sabor de la Navidad
programme.desc: Una pequeña empresa familiar de Rompope enfrenta una encrucijada cuando una transnacional decide cerrar sus puertas en plena temporada navideña. Gregorio, un ambicioso ejecutivo, es el encargado de supervisar el cierre de la empresa local. Pero, al llegar, es recibido con calidez y hospitalidad por los trabajadores de la empresa, especialmente por Erica, la directora de la planta, que cree que su intención es aumentar la producción. Poco a poco Gregorio se sumerge en la magia de la comunidad, comenzando a cuestionar sus propias lealtades y enamorándose del lugar y de Erica. Gregorio terminará enfrentando a su empresa para salvar a la embotelladora y a sus trabajadores y así ganarse el corazón de Erica.

programme.title: Black Gunn
programme.desc: A black militant group robs a Mafia bookie joint and also steals the incriminating ledgers which, in turn, prompts retaliation from the mob.

programme.title: All My Loved Ones
programme.desc: Told from the perspective of man reflecting on his childhood in Prague in the early years of World War 2 and the eventual destruction of his family as the Nazis rise to power.

programme.title: Cannibal Holocaust
programme.desc: An anthropologist heads a rescue party into the South American jungle to find a missing film team making a documentary on cannibal tribes but can only return with their footage, which reveals their crueler intentions.

programme.title: Blood Money
programme.desc: A martial artist joins a hard-hitting gunfighter in the search for treasure while bandits step into their way.

programme.title: The Revenge of Frankenstein
programme.desc: Baron Frankenstein escapes from the guillotine and goes to Germany. There, he names himself Dr. Stein and plans to restart his experiments by using parts of dead bodies.

programme.title: Satan's Slave
programme.desc: A young girl is caught up in a devil cult run by her evil uncle and cousin. She can trust no one and even people she thought were dead comes back to haunt her.

programme.title: Beat the Devil
programme.desc: On their way to Africa are a group of rogues who hope to get rich there, and a seemingly innocent British couple. They meet and things happen...

programme.title: A Farewell to Arms
programme.desc: An American ambulance driver and an English nurse fall in love in Italy during World War I.

programme.title: The Stepfather
programme.desc: After murdering his entire family, a man remarries a widow with a teenage daughter in another town and prepares to do it all over again.

programme.title: Satanico Pandemonium
programme.desc: A young nun is tempted by visions of forbidden sexual fantasies to cross over to Satan.

programme.title: New Year's Day
programme.desc: A man returns to his sublet apartment to find the previous tenants, three offbeat young women, still in residence, under the mistaken belief that they have the apartment until the end of New Year's Day.

programme.title: The Masque of the Red Death
programme.desc: A European prince terrorizes the local peasantry while using his castle as a refuge against the "Red Death" plague that stalks the land.

programme.title: Demons
programme.desc: A group of random people are invited to a screening of a mysterious movie, only to find themselves trapped in the theater with ravenous demons.

programme.title: The Beyond
programme.desc: A young woman inherits an old hotel in Louisiana where after a series of supernatural 'accidents', she learns that the building was built over one of the entrances to Hell.

programme.title: Shivers
programme.desc: The residents of a suburban high-rise apartment building are being infected by a strain of parasites that turn them into mindless, sex-crazed fiends out to infect others by the slightest sexual contact.

programme.title: Day of Redemption
programme.desc: Small-town retired sheriff Frank Everly finds his life on the skids after his wife Mary is murdered by the ruthless maniac Vincent Pope.

programme.title: Frightmare
programme.desc: After escaping a death sentence for her hideous crimes, a seemingly rehabilitated woman settles in an isolated farmhouse with her husband, only to ache, once more, for blood, and a crash-course in surgery. Is, indeed, her old self back?

programme.title: Sebastiane
programme.desc: Reassigned to a lowly outpost, a Roman guard's Christian beliefs clash with his gay commander's desire for closeness. Being tortured becomes pleasurable.

programme.title: Alice and the Vampire Queen

Camila reacts and demands that he keep his word. Max's condition is stable but delicate. Camila goes to the hospital where Astrid tries to attack her.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Ezequiel agrees to help her in exchange for theirs being a real marriage and having a child. Camila executes her plans without his help and leaves. Rosa Blanco told Mother Isabel the whole truth. Disappointed with her daughter's marriage to one of her worst enemies.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Camila looks for excuses to delay the wedding; Elda and Luciano conclude that only Rosa Blanco can stop this madness. Fausto devises a plan to assassinate Ezequiel, at the exit of the church, and also to eliminate Rosa Blanco at once.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Camila is about to give up her revenge and leave with Max, but when she learns of Rosa Blanco's return, she changes her decision. Ezequiel, angry, prepares an intimate dinner, only with Camila, where he will see the deceit and betrayal.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Upon finding Max and Camila embracing, Octavia asks Camila to leave Ezequiel because she loves him. Camila rejects this request because it interferes with her plans and interests. In a play on words with Camila, Ezequiel tries to unmask the betrayal.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Max kisses Camila and begs her to run away together. They are surprised by Ezequiel who hatefully puts a gun to his son's forehead and hits him. Fausto gives Anton the last instructions to eliminate Ezequiel but Torrealba arrives. The wedding ends. A shot is heard.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Total chaos in the church after the shooting. Max is wounded. Ezequiel, takes her by the arm and leads her away, although he feels sorry for his son. Fausto and Roger are the protagonists of this thwarted murder. Ezequiel and Camila tell each other harsh truths.

programme.desc: Steve about dealing with injuries, the start of Inviolate, his very first compositions, how you deal with adversity, Frank Zappa, depression in 20s, Flex-able, removing expectations, Knappsack, genuine inspiration, allowing your creative self to flourish, fantasy goals vs passion, being careful with your ego, getting in toch with your emotions, Avalancha, how he generally writes music, Sandman Cloud Mist, working on new techniques, working with the Metropole Orchestra, Eddie Van Halen.

programme.title: Adam, Jack, and Ryan Part 1
programme.desc: Adam, Jack, and Ryan about their parent’s support, busking on the streets of New York, developing as songwriters, a DIY approach, Disney, the importance of aesthetics, Weak, trying to surprise each other, The Office, Drama, the importance of being relatable

programme.title: 2Cellos Luka and Stjepan Part1
programme.desc: Stjepan and Luka about the first movies they saw in theaters, growing up with soundtracks, the album Score, working with the London Symphony Orchestra, making people fall in love with the cello, staying true to themselves, energetic live shows, connecting to the audience, the importance of humor, compiling the album, composing an original score

programme.title: Agnes Obel interview
programme.desc: Agnes about playing piano at an early age, starting to write her own songs, lyrics. and melodies, tapping into the stream of inspiration, a great sense of freedom, Myopia, Camera’s Rolling, playing with pitch, knowing when you’re on the right track, experimenting with her voice, vocals vs instrumentals

programme.title: Adam, Jack, and Ryan Part 2
programme.desc: Adam, Jack, and Ryan about their parent’s support, busking on the streets of New York, developing as songwriters, a DIY approach, Disney, the importance of aesthetics, Weak, trying to surprise each other, The Office, Drama, the importance of being relatable

programme.title: Blind Melon interview - Rogers Stevens and Christopher Thorn
programme.desc: Rogers and Christopher the early years of the band, realizing their dreams, Shannon Hoon filming the band all the time, the documentary All I Can Say, watching the footage for the first time, who they were back then, the night Shannon died, bittersweet moments, what kind of person Shannon was, how his mom reacted to the film, Change and Shannon’s voice, the randomness of life, how they handled Shannon’s death.

programme.title: Japanese Breakfast interview - Michelle Zauner
programme.desc: Michelle about writing her book ‘Crying in H Mart: A Memoir’ vs writing a song, writing about something new on her new album Jubilee, 2019 being a good year for her, self-imposed pressure, why people might like her music, Posing In Bondage, Kokomo Indiana, delving into the Beatles, her thoughts on success.

programme.title: UB40 interview - Robin Campbell
programme.desc: Robin about the first Baggariddim album, revisiting the format on Bigga Baggariddim, picking who to work with, three songs with House of Shem, ideas left over from For The Many, the state of reggae music today, the songwriting process, Kioko, not making the same music as their father, music reflecting the mood of the people, political songs and barely seeing any social change, his brother Ali leaving the band, no longer speaking to his brother, future plans.

programme.title: Epica interview - Simone Simons
programme.desc: Simone about a forced sabbatical, what keeps her busy these days, the starting point of the new album Omega, writing together in the same room, finding the musical direction, revisiting Design Your Universe, The Skeleton Key, dreams and nightmares, fame vs privacy, Omega being a very diverse album, the Omega point, light vs darkness, Freedom – The Wolves Within, looking back at their earlier work, working with Ayreon on Transitus.

programme.title: P.J. Morton interview
programme.desc: P.J. about the music he grew up with, the first song he ever wrote, his early career and learning about the industry, delving into production, his sound, digging deeper on Watch The Sun, his computer crashing, how the lockdowns influenced the album, Be Like Water, working with Nas and Stevie Wonder, Please Don’t Walk Away, catharsis through songwriting

programme.title: DMA's interview - Tommy O'Dell
programme.desc: Tommy about their show at the Brixton Academy and Liam Gallagher, finding his voice, the album Glow, dance elements, writing lyrics, Silver, staying true to yourself, ambition, not trying to please everyone, Never Before, Criminals and pop, songs that evolve on the road, Life is a Game of Changing, what he learned as a frontman.

programme.title: Beth Hart interview
programme.desc: Beth about learning from gardening, magical moments, addressing personal issues, facing your problems and taking responsibility, singing Led Zeppelin songs, healing through music, recording vocals, Stairway To Heaven and No Quarter, getting honest feedback, other artists she would like to cover, writing new songs of her own, trying new things, being willing to fail and learn, her love for the Netherlands.

programme.title: Alvaro Soler interview
programme.desc: Álvaro about his new album Magia, contrast in his music, summer holiday memories, positive songs, getting back into producing, experimentation in the writing process, displaying his diversity, En Tu Piel, writing from experience, Tipo Normal, feeling useless without live shows, the title Magia

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about his album Zeros, finding his place in music, playfulness, making observations about society, a positive sense of humanity, Daniel You’re Still a Child, The Social Dilemma documentary, turning off his notifications, the good and bad of social media, organic and raw sounds, good mistakes, capturing the right energy on the album, trusting yourself as a musician, taking control, finally getting the album out, his favorite lyric on the album.

programme.title: Interview with Carrie Underwood
programme.desc: An Interview with Carrie Underwood

programme.title: Fish interview
programme.desc: Fish about keeping busy during luckdown, working on the Weltschmerz album, Script for a Jester’s Tear saving his ass, growing vegetables, looking for silver linings, the global economy, the health services, climate change, where the idea for Weltschmerz came from, his character driven style of writing, mental health, Grace of God, his retirement from music, Marillion getting too big, knowing what he wants to make, taking his time, being tough on his own lyrics, leaving people wanting more, doing a double album, never having been financially motivated, doing exactly what you want.

programme.title: Jason Mraz and his cat
programme.desc: Jason about feeling priveledged during social distancing, Gratitude, taking the good with the bad, using music to combat depression, what makes a song great, reggae music, his new album Look For The Good, You Do You, self-acceptance and mindfulness, our common humanity.

programme.title: St. Vincent interview
programme.desc: Annie about how she started in music, creative expression, the sound of the early 70s, writing for her new album Daddy’s Home, writing about flawed people, Somebody Like Me, finding stillness for the first time, not worrying about the commercial side, signing an autograph in prison, why she decided to write about the incarceration of her father, the Wurlitzer, working with Jack Antonoff, the various ways of writing songs, knowing when a song is done, performing at SNL.

programme.title: Cindy Blackman interview
programme.desc: Cindy about The Quarantine Blues, a chance to reset, becoming better humans, her love for the drums, always looking to improve, singing a lot on the new album Give The Drummer Some, We Came To Play, Mother Earth, sharing music, bringing jazz to more people, not putting music into boxes, inspiration, the incredible jazz musicians she learned from, enjoying the little things.

programme.title: James Arthur interview
programme.desc: James about music as a sanctuary, anxiety, his first real song Grey Skies, his songwriting roots, the new record You, letting go of pressure, reinventing himself, Marine Parade, the beauty of being a solo artist, leaving songs open for interpretation, the title track You, being fine with who you are, how he sees success, Glastonbury.

programme.title: Interview with Damien Jurado
programme.desc: An Interview with Damien Jurado

programme.title: Steven Wilson interview
programme.desc: Steven about releasing an album during the pandemic, falling out of love with the guitar, the origins of his new album The Future Bites, living in an electronic world, Eddie van Halen, King Ghost, an exciting songwriting process, making the characters he writes about believable, creativity and technology, the internet changing human nature, the decline of truth and reality, positive change, the year 2032 an consumer culture, curiosity being under threat.

programme.title: Interview with Bring Me The Horizon
programme.desc: An Interview with Bring Me The Horizon

programme.title: Interview with Blossoms
programme.desc: An Interview with Blossoms

programme.title: Bedrugs and PurplePill sing Wave
programme.desc: Bedrugs and PurplePill sing Wave

programme.title: Interview with Billie Eilish
programme.desc: An Interview with Billie Eilish

programme.title: Countain Crows interview - Adam Duritz
programme.desc: Adam about visiting his friends farm in England, shaving his head, starting on the Butter Miracle EP, music being a personal thing for him, Tall Grass, the evolution of his songwriting, the ghosts from your childhood, learning how to live, a screw-up with the release, working on a second Butter Miracle suite, keeping true to the song, a trumpet solo, the album getting so much support, feeling responsible for his crew.

programme.title: Guy Sebastian interview
programme.desc: Guy about coping with the global pandemic, how Australia is handling it, a historically significant time, reflecting on his life and career, realizing what’s important, Before I Go, a messy management betrayal, creativity during lockdown, silver linings, adding positivity to the world, the song Choir for his friend who passed away, a beautiful moment, Standing With You, the importance of mental health, having his sons on the album, gaining strength from the people around him, Believer, T.R.U.T.H

programme.title: Blood Red Shoes interview - Steven Ansell
programme.desc: Steven about not fitting in in Brighton, the punk spirit, dealing with the lockdown, Laura learning to drive, the tone of the new album Ghosts On Tape, MORBID FASCINATION, stripped down tracks, lyric writing, I AM NOT YOU, not being able to play live, pride for what they have accomplished, the secret of longevity, serial killer podcasts and documentaries.

programme.title: Larkin Poe_interview
programme.desc: Rebecca and Megan about playing for change, the power of music, unlearning some of their musical upbringing, trusting themselves, forging their own path, five years of growth, going to Nashville to record Blood Harmony, the art of pre-production, sibling harmonies, still surprising each other, ambition

programme.title: Joe Satriani interview
programme.desc: Joe about when he was still a beginner on guitar, working hard to get better, NYC in the early 70s, the surrealness of his career, teaching Steve Vai, finding “work-arounds” as a guitar player, Eddie van Halen, The Elephants of Mars, experimentation, composing songs over the internet, songs coming together organically, a song inspired by Questlove, Randy Rhoads and what keeps inspiring him.

programme.title: Eefje de Visser interview
programme.desc: Eefje over haar nieuwe plaat Bitterzoet, muziek voor in de auto, schrijven vanuit piano, haar thuisstudio, niet te braaf willen zijn, een internationaal gevoel, altijd beginnen bij de muziek, kritisch zijn op haar eigen teksten, beeldvorming, tegenstellingen, vluchten uit de realiteit, verloren potentie, zelf-bewustzijn, vol inspiratie zitten.

programme.title: Jean-Michel Jarre interview
programme.desc: Jean-Michel about Welcome To The Other Side, a virtual Notre Dame, the impact of the pandemic on music, innovations in music technology, binaural recording, VR and augmented reality as new forms of expression, the value of music, respecting intellectual property, this being only the beginning of the digital age, artificial intelligence, Ray Charles and Pierre Soulages, lessons from his mother, a street in Lyon being named after his mother

programme.title: Best of the Bloomberg Women, Money & Power Event
programme.desc: For a second year, the Bloomberg Women, Money & Power event in London brings together the most influential female voices in finance from around the world to debate and discuss the biggest themes facing the future of business. This special Bloomberg program highlights the event's biggest interviews and news makers.

programme.title: Bloomberg: The China Show
programme.desc: "Bloomberg: The China Show" is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter.

programme.title: Insight with Haslinda Amin
programme.desc: In a volatile and unpredictable world, the show will be the definitive guide for the global news audience to get the complete picture on the biggest story of the day. With news making executives, officials and thought-leaders from the world of business, politics and academia we will explore a story through probing interviews and nuanced conversations. The hour of programming will also highlight the most relevant stories from India which is currently one of the hottest investment destinations, but also has compelling stories that play into the Bloomberg's priority issues such as Climate change, Diversity and Technological innovation.

programme.title: Bloomberg Horizons Middle East & Africa
programme.desc: A spotlight on the fast paced growth and major deals happening across the Middle East and Africa. Linking the market drivers from overnight in the US and across Asia into the region's trading day, with deep dive analysis of the top business, energy and geopolitical stories shaping the decisions of traders across the Middle East, Africa and beyond.

programme.title: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe
programme.desc: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

programme.title: Bloomberg The Opening Trade
programme.desc: The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game.

programme.title: The Pulse with Francine Lacqua
programme.desc: The Pulse with Francine Lacqua is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

programme.title: Bloomberg Brief
programme.desc: Bloomberg Brief delivers the market news, data and analysis you need to set your agenda.

programme.title: Bloomberg Surveillance
programme.desc: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern have the economy and global markets "under surveillance". Their daily conversations with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond cover the latest in business, investment, and geopolitics. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day.

programme.title: Bloomberg Open Interest
programme.desc: Bloomberg Open Interest with Matt Miller and Dani Burger — delivers the market-moving news you need to know to get a jump start on the US trading day.

programme.title: Bloomberg Tech
programme.desc: Bloomberg Tech is the only daily live technology program with a focus on breaking news, market-moving reporting and analysis of global technology companies and stories. The program brings the audience interviews from the biggest names in the business, offering in-depth analysis and critical insights.

programme.title: Bloomberg Markets
programme.desc: Bloomberg Markets is focused on bringing you the most important global business and breaking markets news and information as it happens.

programme.title: Bloomberg Balance of Power
programme.desc: Bloomberg Balance of Power focuses on politics and policies on Capitol Hill, in President Trump's administration, the federal agencies and the courts.

programme.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily
programme.desc: Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec bring you reporting from the magazine that helps global leaders stay ahead, plus insight on the people, companies and trends shaping today's complex economy.

programme.title: Bloomberg The Close
programme.desc: Romaine Bostick and Katie Greifeld break down the day's top market-moving stories and trading action around the closing bell.

programme.title: Bloomberg Balance of Power
programme.desc: Bloomberg Balance of Power focuses on politics and policies on Capitol Hill, in President Trump's administration, the federal agencies and the courts.

programme.title: Businessweek Convenes: Black Leaders Face the DEI Backlash

programme.title: World Sleep Day special: China's sleep economy 'awakening' new consumer trends
programme.desc:
This episode of BizTalk explores China's fast-growing sleep economy – from smart mattresses and sleep aids to tracking technology and health management, the demand for better sleep is on the rise.
CGTN's Lincoln Humphries speaks with Aleksey Efremov, senior vice president of IKEA China; Wang Jin, leader of McKinsey's Life Sciences & Healthcare Practice in China; and David Yuen, managing director of TEMPUR China, on what’s driving this trend.

programme.title: Conversations on Asia's shared future as Boao Forum 2026 concludes
programme.desc: The Boao Forum for Asia 2026 Annual Conference draws to a close on Friday. As global economic uncertainty continues to rise, how can Asia build greater consensus and expand avenues for cooperation? Which topics at this year's forum resonated the most and left a lasting impression? At the close of the forum, CGTN and SSTV reporters gather for an in-depth conversation—reflecting on key moments and sharing insights.

programme.title: Investing in China to Share the Future
programme.desc: Against the backdrop of a new landscape of globalization, the strategies of foreign-invested enterprises in China have undergone a profound transformation. The continued growth of China and Asia has enabled even greater possibilities for foreign enterprises. programme.title: Around China: Explore Lijiang's vibrant nighttime economy with Naxi culture
programme.desc: In recent years, Lijiang, Yunnan Province, has been leveraging its unique local resources to enrich and elevate its nighttime economy. By promoting activities such as nighttime dining, scenic views, and evening performances, Lijiang has unleashed vibrant consumer energy, attracting a growing number of tourists. Join CGTN Reporter Zhu Zhu to immerse in the Naxi ethnic wear, taking part in a bonfire party at Sifang Street, and explore Lijiang’s nighttime economy firsthand!

programme.desc: Against the backdrop of a new landscape of globalization, the strategies of foreign-invested enterprises in China have undergone a profound transformation. The continued growth of China and Asia has enabled even greater possibilities for foreign enterprises. CGTN host Lily Lyu moderates the panel discussion themed “Investing in China to Share the Future” at the Boao Forum for Asia this year, engaging in discussions with representatives on how foreign enterprises can position China and Asia as key hubs for innovation through deep, multi-dimensional integration. #BoaoForum2026#

programme.title: Inside the Cai Family Residence: Tracing a century in Hainan
programme.desc: As the Boao Forum for Asia 2026 enters its second day, there's more to explore beyond the conference halls. Follow CGTN to the Cai Family Residence to discover the stories of overseas Chinese and get a glimpse of the island's transformation over the past century, as well as Hainan's ties with the wider region. #BoaoForum2026 #DiscoverHainan

programme.title: World Sleep Day special: China's sleep economy 'awakening' new consumer trends
programme.desc:
This episode of BizTalk explores China's fast-growing sleep economy – from smart mattresses and sleep aids to tracking technology and health management, the demand for better sleep is on the rise.
CGTN's Lincoln Humphries speaks with Aleksey Efremov, senior vice president of IKEA China; Wang Jin, leader of McKinsey's Life Sciences & Healthcare Practice in China; and David Yuen, managing director of TEMPUR China, on what’s driving this trend.

programme.title: Around China: Explore Lijiang's vibrant nighttime economy with Naxi culture
programme.desc: In recent years, Lijiang, Yunnan Province, has been leveraging its unique local resources to enrich and elevate its nighttime economy. By promoting activities such as nighttime dining, scenic views, and evening performances, Lijiang has unleashed vibrant consumer energy, attracting a growing number of tourists. Join CGTN Reporter Zhu Zhu to immerse in the Naxi ethnic wear, taking part in a bonfire party at Sifang Street, and explore Lijiang’s nighttime economy firsthand!

programme.title: Dances with the Wind
programme.desc: ‘Fury Dance’ is a story about a Korean protest dancer, Sam-hun Lee. He fought for the democratization of South Korea in the ‘80’s through dance, while giving up his own dream to become a ballerino. The film takes the viewer through prominent events in South Korean history, as Sam-hun dances to soothe the souls of victims who were killed by the Korean national violence during the past 30 years. During the 1980 Gwangju Massacre however, Sam-hun developed a panic disorder. So he crosses through the Eurasian rail with difficulty when invited to attend a festival to dance in France. Through his journey, he attempts to overcome his claustrophobic fears in France, revisits his lost dream of becoming a ballerino in Russia, and dances for the Holocaust victims in Poland. Documented for 15 years, this film is dedicated to those who lost their noble lives while fighting for freedom against the unjust political power.

programme.title: 1st Bite
programme.desc: Set on a tropical island in Thailand, the strange plight of a beleaguered chef who, while romancing a mysterious woman, discovers the diabolical Zen of cooking. Following a near death escape, he returns to Montreal and falls hard for the woman of his life who unfortunately craves only his cooking but not his loving. Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: Frank & Fearless

Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: Frank & Fearless
programme.desc: An aging reprobate, a rural boy, a large dog and an orphaned baby rhino set out to stop the rhino slaughter. Their quest buffets them between high comedy and searing tragedy, until they end up an inspiration and a conscience to a world in need of heroes.

programme.title: Making Out
programme.desc: A screenwriter and self-proclaimed hopeless romantic meets a beautiful actress and they decide to act out their ideal love scenarios. When real feelings start to jump off the page and become real will he tell her how he feels? They're in love, probably.

programme.title: Beach Babe Bingo
programme.desc: The water is cool and the girls are hot, what more could you want? Jump in and go for a swim, then wash up for a fun night out because the beach has nothing but sand and babes.

programme.title: Running Funny
programme.desc: Michael and Eddie are two broke college graduates who rent an “apartment” from Stan, a cantankerous blind war veteran. As they begin their tumultuous transition into the real world, they quickly discover that finding a job will be more complex than securing their degrees.

programme.title: Cabin of Errors
programme.desc: When Peter and Nancy split up, their friends plot to bring them back together during a trip to a cabin. But things go hilariously wrong when Peter comes to the cabin with other intentions. A modern day romantic comedy farce.

programme.title: Cabin of Errors
programme.desc: When Peter and Nancy split up, their friends plot to bring them back together during a trip to a cabin. But things go hilariously wrong when Peter comes to the cabin with other intentions. A modern day romantic comedy farce.

programme.title: The Malibu Beach Vampires
programme.desc: In addition to the traditional bloodsuckers, there are other kinds of vampires, you know...such as some politicians, military people, and evangelists.

programme.title: La carta astral de Pedro Sanchez y Begoña Gómez I Begoña es la que manda I Ministerio de Brujas
programme.desc:
Este martes en Ministerio de Brujas (19:00h España, en Canal Barro), las ministras abrieron los portales del poder para leer las cartas astrales de Pedro Sánchez y Begoña Gómez 🔥. Lo que descubrieron dejó a todos con la boca abierta: ♑ Él, un hombre obsesionado con el poder, encantador pero peligroso en su ingenuidad. ♌ Ella, inteligente, estratega y con los pantalones del vínculo.
Además, en la Hoguera semanal ardieron los males cotidianos: 🚗 los Uber que nunca llegan, 😤 la gente que mastica con la boca abierta, ⚧ y un intenso debate sobre identidad y transparencia en las relaciones.
La bruja invitada de la semana fue Mercedes Jorqueira, voluntaria de la DANA, que contó en directo su experiencia ayudando en plena catástrofe. En el Departamento de Cinematografía Zodíacal, se recomendaron películas y series de desastres como Chernóbil y Lo imposible. Y en el Archivo de Brujas Quemadas, se honró la figura inmortal de Mercedes Sosa 🎶, voz y fuego eterno de América Latina.
✨ Ministerio de Brujas — el programa donde el poder se lee en las estrellas, se quema en la hoguera y se transforma en conciencia. Todos los martes a las 19:00h (España) en YouTube @arroba.barro.

programme.title: Afrontar la adolescencia de tus hijos, Duelo emocional de las madre, Momento de DESmadre Podcast

programme.title: MINISTERIO DE BRUJAS: Carta Astral de Los Javis, Caras de Bélmez, Mal de Ojo y Venus en Escorpio.
programme.desc:
Bienvenid@s al Ministerio de Brujas, el único programa donde la magia tiene reglamento, las dudas tienen expediente y la intuición legisla sin oposición. En este episodio, grabado en vivo en@CanalBarro el aquelarre vino encendido.
🔥 PROTOCOLO DE LA HOGUERA Quemamos todo lo que necesita transformarse: los crush imposibles de tu ideología opuesta, la gente que vive diciendo “no”, los silencios incómodos del WhatsApp y esa tortura mental llamada “debería estar haciendo algo”. Aquí el fuego purifica… o al menos nos da permiso para reírnos.
💋 SECRETARÍA DE VENUS EN TANGA Nos adentramos en el magnetismo oscuro de Venus en Escorpio: deseo extremo, intensidad emocional, tabúes, renacer afectivo y ese erotismo que ve en la piel ajena un archivo confidencial. Además, tiramos una carta del tarot erótico para leer el clima del deseo.
🎬 DIRECCIÓN GENERAL DE CINEMATOGRAFÍA ZODIAZAL La Dra. Fernanda Garrido trae cine, signos y elementos. Películas que dialogan con el cielo y con nuestras crisis de identidad astrológica. Cine como brújula, literal.
✨ CLIMA ASTRAL & MITOS ChongaZen explica los movimientos planetarios y luego destapamos dos clásicos del misterio: • El Mal de Ojo: desde Mesopotamia hasta TikTok. • El espejo roto y los 7 años de mala suerte: Roma, magia y supersticiones que siguen vivitas.
👁 SUBSECRETARÍA DE MISTERIOS: LAS CARAS DE BÉLMEZ El caso paranormal más famoso de España: rostros que aparecen en el suelo, análisis forenses, sellos notariales, restos humanos bajo la casa y un misterio que ni la ciencia cerró. Brutal.
💘 DEPARTAMENTO DE ESTRELLAS Y SÁBANAS Analizamos la compatibilidad cósmica de Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi. Cartas natales sobre la mesa. La química astral nunca miente.
🔥 BRUJAS QUEMADAS O EXILIADAS La activista Tarana Burke, madre del movimiento Me Too, entra en nuestros Archivos Clasificados. Poder, voz y reparación.
💬 Cierre con los Sindicatos Zodiacales Acuario pide dejar de ser llamado frí@, Cáncer pregunta si hace falta sentir TODO, y Libra… Libra reclama coherencia universal.
📌 Suscríbete, activa la campanita y envíanos tu expediente esotérico a nuestro mail. 📌 Ministerio de Brujas — todos los martes a las 19h en Canal Barro.

The cigar is a blend of aged tobacco with an Ecuador Sumatra wrapper, Honduran Candela binder, and a mix of other fillers. They compare it with the Los Statos Maduro, which has a similar vibe but is spicier with notes of cocoa, and the H. Upmann 175th Anniversary, which is also a "very good" cigar and a medium to full body smoke. They then move on to pair the cigars with whiskey, trying a 20-year-old whiskey and an American whiskey, with each having different notes and profiles.

programme.sub-title: Creekside Cigar Co - The Future Of Cigar Humidity?
programme.desc: In this episode of the Creekside Podcast, Dave and Noah are joined by Abe Wolke, founder of Valet Humidity, to discuss his new humidity control brand and his journey from product design and tech to cigar accessories. Abe shares how the visual appeal of his product, designed with aesthetics in mind, initially caught Dave's attention, and explains Valet's approach to humidity levels, offering packs for aging (65%), airtight containers (69%), standard use (72%), and "culturing" (75%) for a unique "funky" cigar experience. They also explore the importance of human craftsmanship in cigars, the value of personalized branding for retailers, and the unique community spirit within the cigar industry, while smoking a United Cigars Gold Star.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Horses in art
programme.desc: 2026 is the Year of the Horse, but what does the animal represent in Chinese culture? Join us as we follow the horse through art: How a sculptor captures the horse's beauty? A Peking Opera performer reveals how to become horse and rider on stage. Xu Beihong's iconic ink paintings and the spirit they inspired across a nation. Ethnic Mongolian dance, expressing the freedom and joy of riding This Year of the Horse: be bold. Pick up the reins, find your herd and charge ahead.

programme.title: Dazzling Lion Dance
programme.desc: Experience this ‘very Chinese time of your life’. Have you ever seen a lion that radiates a spectrum of colors? On the streets of Zhanjiang, Guangdong, an extraordinary lion dance performance is heating up the celebrations for the 2026 Chinese New Year.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Boxing through the Holidays
programme.desc: Staying active during the holidays can be a challenge, especially with all the food and festivities tempting you at every turn. But what if you could sneak in a workout without having to hit the gym? Next, join Lyne Lin and Jason as they show you how to stay active during the holiday season.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Saddling up for new adventures with bold neon and traditional ink
programme.desc: This Lunar New Year, horses are set to steal the show as the Chinese zodiac migrates over to a new animal. But for one Beijing artist, born under this very sign, painting these trusty steeds is more than just a tradition – it’s an expression of freedom. Her work fuses explosive neon colors with bold ink lines. So, what drives her to create these galloping beasts?

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha — the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Our lens turns to the "Xiangjiang Ladies" who work in Changsha’s high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city’s innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha’s distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: Celadon Ou Music
programme.desc: Celadon ou music is also called "bowl music.” The reason is that the ancient Chinese word for bowl sounds like ou. The music originated simply as improvised rhythms tapped out on bowls. It was this spontaneity that made celadon ou so popular. Celadon ou music was at the height of its popularity over 1,100 years ago. But with time, it faded from history. At one point, it was even on the verge of being lost forever. After hundreds of years of obscurity, it re-emerged at the end of last century.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: Calm, Cool & Cultured: How one local jewelry designer is reimagining the Chinese zodiac horse
programme.desc: As the Year of the Horse gallops into view, a Chinese designer who was herself born in this zodiac year is putting a fresh spin on how we view this cherished beast of burden—one jewel at a time. Shen Li paid Zhang Jilin a visit to explore how she blends her vibrant energy with quiet elegance in her craft.

programme.title: The Sichuan Zhuqin
programme.desc: Sichuan Zhuqin is a national intangible cultural heritage in China. Nowadays, its performances are constantly innovated, with new styles such as ensemble emerging. Creators have broken traditional performance methods, integrating Zhuqin with traditional Chinese instruments like the guzheng and erhu, and also experimenting with contemporary music forms such as rap and folk rock, aiming to make this traditional art appeal to more young audiences.

programme.title: Unbridled: Graffiti artist taps animal spirit to spray city with zodiac energy
programme.desc: As the advent of the Year of the Horse brings a new kind of energy to 2026, Ma Xiao, aka. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: The Tongliang Dragon Dance
programme.desc: The Tongliang Dragon Dance is a traditional performance art rooted in Chongqing’s Tongliang District, characterized by its elaborate dragon props and dynamic choreography. Originating in the Ming Dynasty and flourishing during the Qing, this vibrant folk tradition has regained its brilliance in modern times and earned international acclaim. The dance consists of two main branches: the dragon lantern dance—featuring forms like the Grand Wriggling Dragon, the Fire Dragon, and the Straw Dragon—and the festive lantern dance, which includes acts such as “Carp Leaps Over the Dragon Gate,” “Mudfish Eating Dumplings,” and “Three Dragons.” Steeped in cultural symbolism, the Tongliang Dragon Dance expresses values of unity, vitality, and harmony with nature. While a few iconic forms like the Fire Dragon remain widely recognized, many others are on the verge of extinction and in urgent need of preservation. In this episode, the host travels to Chongqing to meet with four inheritors of the Tongliang Dragon Dance. Through their stories, we uncover the rich legacy of this dazzling tradition, explore the deep roots of dragon culture in the region, and trace the origins of one of China’s most awe-inspiring folk arts.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Zodiac Girls’ New Year Heights
programme.desc: This zodiac year, the ancient idiom "MaDaoChengGong" promises that success will gallop right to your door. Our culture host, Julian Waghann, saddled up to meet some young equestrians whose personal quests might just teach us all how to leap into our own lucky year! Take a look.

programme.title: The Sichuan Zhuqin
programme.desc: Sichuan Zhuqin is a national intangible cultural heritage in China. Nowadays, its performances are constantly innovated, with new styles such as ensemble emerging. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: The Tongliang Dragon Dance
programme.desc: The Tongliang Dragon Dance is a traditional performance art rooted in Chongqing’s Tongliang District, characterized by its elaborate dragon props and dynamic choreography. Originating in the Ming Dynasty and flourishing during the Qing, this vibrant folk tradition has regained its brilliance in modern times and earned international acclaim. The dance consists of two main branches: the dragon lantern dance—featuring forms like the Grand Wriggling Dragon, the Fire Dragon, and the Straw Dragon—and the festive lantern dance, which includes acts such as “Carp Leaps Over the Dragon Gate,” “Mudfish Eating Dumplings,” and “Three Dragons.” Steeped in cultural symbolism, the Tongliang Dragon Dance expresses values of unity, vitality, and harmony with nature. While a few iconic forms like the Fire Dragon remain widely recognized, many others are on the verge of extinction and in urgent need of preservation. In this episode, the host travels to Chongqing to meet with four inheritors of the Tongliang Dragon Dance. Through their stories, we uncover the rich legacy of this dazzling tradition, explore the deep roots of dragon culture in the region, and trace the origins of one of China’s most awe-inspiring folk arts.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1

programme.title: Saddling up for new adventures with bold neon and traditional ink
programme.desc: This Lunar New Year, horses are set to steal the show as the Chinese zodiac migrates over to a new animal. programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha — the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city’s innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha’s distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: Celadon Ou Music
programme.desc: Celadon ou music is also called "bowl music.” The reason is that the ancient Chinese word for bowl sounds like ou. The music originated simply as improvised rhythms tapped out on bowls. It was this spontaneity that made celadon ou so popular. Celadon ou music was at the height of its popularity over 1,100 years ago. But with time, it faded from history. At one point, it was even on the verge of being lost forever. After hundreds of years of obscurity, it re-emerged at the end of last century.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. programme.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programme.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China’s national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors—but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: Guqin Music Art
programme.desc: The guqin is an instrument with a history of over 3,000 years. Yet in all that time, its design and sound have remained virtually unchanged. In 2003, the guqin and its music were proclaimed as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. But how has this ancient instrument withstood the musical test of time? How do its slow, gentle melodies resonate in fast-paced modern China? In this episode of The Inheritors, we explore guqin music art’s history, development in modern days, and its future.

programme.title: Huayin Old Tunes: the Earliest Rock and Roll by the Yellow River
programme.desc: Huayin Laoqiang is the name given to a traditional form of shadow puppet show. It translates as “Huayin Old Tunes,” and originated in the chanting of the boatmen working at the confluence of the Yellow, Weihe, and Luohe Rivers, close to the city of Huayin in Shaanxi Province. This chanting evolved into folk songs which, with time, were illustrated with puppet shows. The loud music, rustic instruments, and enthusiastic performances epitomize the way the local people lead their lives.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programme.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China’s national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors—but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: Guqin Music Art
programme.desc: The guqin is an instrument with a history of over 3,000 years. Yet in all that time, its design and sound have remained virtually unchanged. In 2003, the guqin and its music were proclaimed as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. But how has this ancient instrument withstood the musical test of time? How do its slow, gentle melodies resonate in fast-paced modern China? In this episode of The Inheritors, we explore guqin music art’s history, development in modern days, and its future.

programme.title: Calm, Cool & Cultured: How one local jewelry designer is reimagining the Chinese zodiac horse
programme.desc: As the Year of the Horse gallops into view, a Chinese designer who was herself born in this zodiac year is putting a fresh spin on how we view this cherished beast of burden—one jewel at a time. Shen Li paid Zhang Jilin a visit to explore how she blends her vibrant energy with quiet elegance in her craft.

programme.title: Huayin Old Tunes: the Earliest Rock and Roll by the Yellow River
programme.desc: Huayin Laoqiang is the name given to a traditional form of shadow puppet show. It translates as “Huayin Old Tunes,” and originated in the chanting of the boatmen working at the confluence of the Yellow, Weihe, and Luohe Rivers, close to the city of Huayin in Shaanxi Province. This chanting evolved into folk songs which, with time, were illustrated with puppet shows. The loud music, rustic instruments, and enthusiastic performances epitomize the way the local people lead their lives.

programme.title: Unbridled: Graffiti artist taps animal spirit to spray city with zodiac energy
programme.desc: As the advent of the Year of the Horse brings a new kind of energy to 2026, Ma Xiao, aka. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: Quanzhou Puppet Theater: China’s "Pinocchio Adventure"
programme.desc: In the film, the puppet Pinocchio, carved and created by an old carpenter, comes to life as a real human. This episode takes you into the world of Quanzhou String Puppet Theater. programme.desc: Join Tianran He in Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. From sacred mountains and ancient monasteries, to cruising along Nyingchi’s mother river, wandering alpine meadows and savoring stone pot chicken – a beloved local delicacy, Tianran uncovers the beauty of Nyingchi.

programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon – one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: Outkirts of Wenzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He explores Wenzhou’s counties. From geological wonders and daring cliffside stunts at the Yandang Mountains, to rafting along the scenic Nanxi River, to harvesting seaweed and shellfish on the mud flats of the Dongtou Islands, Tianran discovers the ingenious ways the people of Wenzhou have transformed the challenges of living between mountains and seas into their greatest strengths.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. programme.title: Quanzhou Nanyin: A Living Fossil in the History of Chinese Music
programme.desc: Nanyin, also known as “Quanzhou Nanyin,” is an ancient Han Chinese musical tradition whose singing style preserves the time-honored ethnic vocal techniques predating the Tang Dynasty, earning it the title of “a living fossil in the history of Chinese music.” The program features Yegor, a Ukrainian music enthusiast, visiting Master Su Shuyong, a Nanyin inheritor, to hear her decades-long stories of teaching this art. They also tour the Quanzhou Nanyin Troupe, where, led by its artistic director Zhuang Lifen, they learn about the basic performance formats and instruments of Nanyin. Additionally, the episode follows a post-1990s Nanyin performer, Zheng Mingming, as she sips tea with guests at sunset, reflecting on the deep-rooted role Nanyin plays in the daily lives of Quanzhou’s people.

programme.title: Musician keeps Mongolia’s cultural roots embedded and evolving on world stage
programme.desc: Hailing from the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China but having spent over a decade in Beijing, Asr blends the soul of traditional Mongolian music—like the horsehead fiddle and throat singing—with jazz, electronic, and West African influences. As a keyboardist and composer in two boundary-pushing bands, NaraBara and Mola Oddity, he’s brought his unique sound to audiences in Europe and beyond. CGTN reporter Yang Yan sits down with the Mongolian artist to explore how his roots have shaped his musical journey around the world.

programme.title: Celebrating the Corban Festival
programme.desc: Kashgar, situated in the southwest of Xinjiang, was a key stop on the ancient Silk Road. It served as a gateway for trade between China and countries in Asia and Europe. However, it wasn’t only goods that were exchanged on the Silk Road. So, too, were cultures, which merged and flourished. In the 7th century AD, Islam entered China’s western regions along the Silk Road, bringing with it the Corban Festival. With time, Corban became more than a religious festival. It developed into a traditional holiday celebrated by everyone in Kashgar. Corban is as important as New Year. Kashgar locals load their tables with food on this day to reward themselves for a year of hard work. Corban is all about sharing. In the past, rich families would buy extra meat to share with their neighbors and friends. This tradition is still alive in Kashgar today, although it’s practiced not just by the rich, but pretty well everyone.

programme.title: Calm, Cool & Cultured: How one local jewelry designer is reimagining the Chinese zodiac horse
programme.desc: As the Year of the Horse gallops into view, a Chinese designer who was herself born in this zodiac year is putting a fresh spin on how we view this cherished beast of burden—one jewel at a time. Shen Li paid Zhang Jilin a visit to explore how she blends her vibrant energy with quiet elegance in her craft.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas. As such, it is an integral part of Xinjiang culture—and even the culture of the Silk Road. In the episode, the host travels around the Kashgar area, learning about the history and art of Muqam.

programme.title: Unbridled: Graffiti artist taps animal spirit to spray city with zodiac energy
programme.desc: As the advent of the Year of the Horse brings a new kind of energy to 2026, Ma Xiao, aka. Max017 isn’t just adding kaleidoscopic colour to a local wall; he’s charging into the zodiac year of his birth with unbridled energy. By fusing ancient Chinese philosophy with the edgy aesthetics of street graffiti, he is transforming urban slabs of concrete into living tributes to the beauty of the horse—all through the nozzle of a spray can.

programme.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programme.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it’s said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Zodiac Girls’ New Year Heights
programme.desc: This zodiac year, the ancient idiom "MaDaoChengGong" promises that success will gallop right to your door. Our culture host, Julian Waghann, saddled up to meet some young equestrians whose personal quests might just teach us all how to leap into our own lucky year! Take a look.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: Join Tianran He in Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. Fed by the Yarlung Zangbo River and abundant rainfall, this lush subtropical region is home to some of Xizan’g most unique scenery. From sacred mountains and ancient monasteries, to cruising along Nyingchi’s mother river, wandering alpine meadows and savoring stone pot chicken – a beloved local delicacy, Tianran uncovers the beauty of Nyingchi.

programme.title: Horses in art
programme.desc: 2026 is the Year of the Horse, but what does the animal represent in Chinese culture? Join us as we follow the horse through art: How a sculptor captures the horse's beauty? A Peking Opera performer reveals how to become horse and rider on stage. Xu Beihong's iconic ink paintings and the spirit they inspired across a nation. Ethnic Mongolian dance, expressing the freedom and joy of riding This Year of the Horse: be bold. Pick up the reins, find your herd and charge ahead.

programme.title: Dazzling Lion Dance
programme.desc: Experience this ‘very Chinese time of your life’. Have you ever seen a lion that radiates a spectrum of colors? On the streets of Zhanjiang, Guangdong, an extraordinary lion dance performance is heating up the celebrations for the 2026 Chinese New Year.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: Boxing through the Holidays
programme.desc: Staying active during the holidays can be a challenge, especially with all the food and festivities tempting you at every turn. But what if you could sneak in a workout without having to hit the gym? Next, join Lyne Lin and Jason as they show you how to stay active during the holiday season.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon – one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

programme.title: Saddling up for new adventures with bold neon and traditional ink
programme.desc: This Lunar New Year, horses are set to steal the show as the Chinese zodiac migrates over to a new animal. But for one Beijing artist, born under this very sign, painting these trusty steeds is more than just a tradition – it’s an expression of freedom. Her work fuses explosive neon colors with bold ink lines. So, what drives her to create these galloping beasts?

programme.title: Wenzhou
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Wenzhou, southeast China — a city famed for its self-made millionaires. Here he meets the first Chinese shoemaker to expand overseas, and hears the stories of other local entrepreneurs. Along the way, he samples traditional snacks, visits some of China’s oldest lighthouses, and enjoys an evening of Ou Opera. He also learns the craft of papermaking, before heading into the hills to soak in hot springs and wander across ancient covered bridges.

programme.title: YEAR OF THE HORSE Why horses in British and Chinese art still speak to the Year of the Horse today
programme.desc: What does an iconic British racehorse have in common with Chinese ink paintings? Quite a lot, actually. This Year of the Horse, we’re looking at how artists across cultures have captured freedom, movement, and spirit.

programme.title: Outkirts of Wenzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He explores Wenzhou’s counties. From geological wonders and daring cliffside stunts at the Yandang Mountains, to rafting along the scenic Nanxi River, to harvesting seaweed and shellfish on the mud flats of the Dongtou Islands, Tianran discovers the ingenious ways the people of Wenzhou have transformed the challenges of living between mountains and seas into their greatest strengths.

programme.title: Chinese New Year vibe permeates Beijing museums
programme.desc: As people prepare to ring in the Chinese New Year, Beijing's repositories of culture, history and knowledge are launching a wave of exhibitions that weave together threads of tradition, artistry, and symbolism. From the communal joy of folk celebrations to the enduring spirit embodied in the zodiac symbol of the horse, these showcases offer a glimpse into the profundity of Chinese heritage and wisdom, uniting the past with the present.

programme.title: Quanzhou Nanyin: A Living Fossil in the History of Chinese Music
programme.desc: Nanyin, also known as “Quanzhou Nanyin,” is an ancient Han Chinese musical tradition whose singing style preserves the time-honored ethnic vocal techniques predating the Tang Dynasty, earning it the title of “a living fossil in the history of Chinese music.” The program features Yegor, a Ukrainian music enthusiast, visiting Master Su Shuyong, a Nanyin inheritor, to hear her decades-long stories of teaching this art. They also tour the Quanzhou Nanyin Troupe, where, led by its artistic director Zhuang Lifen, they learn about the basic performance formats and instruments of Nanyin. Additionally, the episode follows a post-1990s Nanyin performer, Zheng Mingming, as she sips tea with guests at sunset, reflecting on the deep-rooted role Nanyin plays in the daily lives of Quanzhou’s people.
